summary: This bill raises authorized federal funding levels for IDEA section 619 preschool grants and part C early intervention services by setting specific increasing appropriation amounts for each fiscal year from 2027 through 2031.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes substantial increases in appropriations for IDEA Part C and Section 619 programs, with funding levels rising from hundreds of millions to over $1.7 billion by FY 2031. This directly expands federal government spending on early childhood special education services.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue measures.

While early intervention services can have health-related components, the bill exclusively addresses funding under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), which is an education statute, not healthcare policy.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, border policy, or pathways for non-citizens.
No provisions address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions involve military or defense spending.
No provisions relate to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill funds education services for young children with disabilities but does not address welfare programs, food assistance, or other traditional safety-net entitlements.

The bill specifically increases authorized federal funding for preschool special education (Section 619) and early intervention services (Part C) under IDEA, directly expanding public investment and federal involvement in education for children with disabilities.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance abuse policy.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill increases spending authorizations without any offsetting measures or debt-reduction language, but its primary focus is education funding rather than fiscal policy.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral reform.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address labor rights, unions, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
